solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tavern in Western Peru represented in books

indicators.note: to be represented is to be rendered in a new form, so these letters are rearranged
placing something in another means it sits between that other's outer letters

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for western
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book, so two books give BB

explanation.surface: A South American inn turns up as a setting in some novels.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged W and PERU sit between the two Bs of 'books'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewpub is a bar that brews its own beer on site, a modern kind of tavern.

clue.text: Britpop band extremely rowdy, lacking focus

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: Blur were a leading 1990s Britpop group
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A 1990s pop group behaves wildly and loses concentration.
explanation.walkthrough: Blur, rivals of Oasis, were one of the defining bands of 1990s British guitar pop.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurry photograph or view is out of focus, with edges smeared rather than sharp.

clue.text: After downsizing, Newcastle use bionic footballer

indicators.note: downsizing trims a firm down, so the words are cut at both ends to leave a smaller run inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A cash-strapped Newcastle United turns to a robotic player.
explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle is a city whose famous football club has been through lean spells, which the surface plays on. Eusebio was the great Portuguese striker of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Eusebio, Benfica and Portugal forward and top scorer at the 1966 World Cup, is one of soccer's legends.

clue.text: Photograph yuletide saint and queen outside diner

blocks.note: pic is short for picture
St Nick, Saint Nicholas, is Santa Claus
ER, Elizabeth Regina, placed on the outside end

explanation.surface: Someone takes a snapshot of Santa and the monarch standing beyond a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diner' looks like a roadside restaurant but is a person eating; 'outside' just puts the queen at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnicker eats a meal outdoors, so is one kind of person having a meal.

clue.text: Hospital working to support naughty kids — one in particular

definitions.note: refers back to the naughty kids: one particular naughty child

blocks.note: Barts is St Bartholomew's, a famous London hospital
imps are mischievous children
on means working; in a down clue what supports goes underneath

explanation.surface: A hospital puts on activities for badly behaved children, one child especially.
explanation.walkthrough: Barts is St Bartholomew's Hospital in London. The definition leans on the wordplay: of all naughty kids, one in particular.
explanation.definitionFit: Bart Simpson, the cartoon troublemaker of The Simpsons, is the archetypal mischievous boy on television.

clue.text: Like S&M, perhaps, in old courts?

blocks.note: as means like, in the manner of
S and M, small and medium, are examples of clothing measurements

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether old law courts went in for bondage.
explanation.walkthrough: S&M tempts the reader towards sadomasochism, but here it stands for small and medium on a clothes label.
explanation.definitionFit: The assizes were periodic English county courts, abolished in 1971 and replaced by the Crown Court.

clue.text: Assist with unfinished opera

indicators.note: something left unfinished lacks its ending, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: Aida is Verdi's opera set in ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: Someone lends a hand completing an opera that was left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: Aida is the crossword's favourite opera: Verdi's, four letters, easily trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid someone is to help or support them, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Cancel US sitcom without finale

indicators.note: with no finale there is no closing piece, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: An American hospital comedy series

explanation.surface: A network axes an American comedy before its final episode airs.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrubs ran from 2001 to 2010 and followed junior doctors at a teaching hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is informal for calling it off, so both mean abandon or drop.

clue.text: With energy, Zulu reportedly, enters short country river?

indicators.note: spoken as a radio code word: this word is what operators say for a single letter
to enter is to go inside, so one part is put within another
cut short means docked at the end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the African nation
E is the symbol for energy
Zulu is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for Z

explanation.surface: Energetic Zulu people are said to be moving into a small nation by its waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: Zambia loses its last letter; E and Z go inside, ahead of its final I. The question mark flags that the river and country share a name stem.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zambezi is a major southern African waterway, home of Victoria Falls on the Zambia-Zimbabwe border.

clue.text: Lacking organisation, band is infiltrated by US cops

indicators.note: infiltrators get inside a group, so one piece is slipped into the middle of another

blocks.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist
the Los Angeles Police Department

explanation.surface: A disorganised music group finds American police officers going undercover in its ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but it is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is careless and hurried, done without method or proper order.

clue.text: Rues dunce somehow becoming loose

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters reach the result by an unstated rearrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dim pupil regrets running wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' joins the wordplay to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsecured is not fastened or tied down, so it is free and liable to move.

clue.text: Liquor carrier moves out of Cuba

blocks.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
BA is British Airways, an airline that carries passengers

explanation.surface: A drinks transporter relocates away from Havana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moves' reads as a verb about relocating, but it is a noun: dance moves. BA, British Airways, is the UK's flag carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a ballroom and folk dance of Afro-Cuban origin, its steps coming from the island.

clue.text: One in Temple Bar knocked back first couple of bitters

indicators.note: knocked back means thrown backwards, so the word is read right to left
the first couple are the opening two, so only the leading pair of letters is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening two letters

explanation.surface: Someone in a Temple Bar pub downs the first two pints of bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Temple Bar is Dublin's pub district, and bitter is a British style of ale; but the definition ends at 'Temple', a synagogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is the religious leader of a Jewish congregation, whose synagogue is often called a temple.

clue.text: Weirdly, adores eating fish food

indicators.note: something done weirdly is done oddly, so the letters come out in a strange new order
to eat something is to take it inside, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: taken as written
a dab is a small flatfish

explanation.surface: Someone oddly loves eating fish food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish food' looks like a phrase, but 'fish' is wordplay and 'food' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda bread is an Irish loaf raised with bicarbonate of soda instead of yeast, a staple foodstuff.

clue.text: Betray what’s apparent in anti-vaxxers

definitions.note: cryptic: the word contains a pair of Xs

blocks.note: first meaning: to cheat someone you had pretended to help
second meaning: the word has two Xs in a row, and an X is a cross

explanation.surface: A complaint that vaccine opponents show their true, treacherous colours.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is not about attitudes at all: look at the spelling of 'anti-vaxxers' and its pair of side-by-side Xs.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-cross is to deceive or cheat an ally, a verb meaning to betray.

clue.text: Yank consortium bulldozed American peaks

indicators.note: ground that is bulldozed is churned and pushed around, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American business group flattens a mountain range for development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like a noun for an American, but it is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rocky Mountains form the great range running through western North America, from Canada to New Mexico.

clue.text: Military display is beginning to trouble needleworker

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so just that one is kept

blocks.note: a tattoo is an evening military parade with music, as at Edinburgh
taken as written
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A military parade starts to worry someone who sews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needleworker' suggests embroidery, but the needle is one that inks skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooist works with a needle to put ink under the skin, a witty twist on a sewer.

clue.text: Name of chap on X

blocks.note: a typical man's first name
X is the Roman numeral for ten; in a down clue the first piece sits on top of this

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a man's name is on the social platform X.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name' is a verb here, not a noun, and 'X' is a Roman numeral, not the social network.
explanation.definitionFit: To christen a baby or ship is to give it a name at a ceremony.

clue.text: Very clear decision after taking drugs?

blocks.note: someone who has taken drugs is high
a resolution is a firm decision

explanation.surface: A firm resolve made while stoned seems wonderfully lucid.
explanation.walkthrough: The state of being drugged comes first in the answer even though the clue puts it last.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-resolution image or screen shows fine detail sharply, so it looks extremely sharp and crisp.

clue.text: Picked up famous dog’s rubber ring

indicators.note: picked up as on a radio means heard, so the answer is a word that sounds like this one

blocks.note: Gromit is the clever dog of the Wallace and Gromit films

explanation.surface: Someone collects a well-known dog's rubber toy ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallace and Gromit are the plasticine cheese-loving inventor and his silent dog in Aardman's British animations.
explanation.definitionFit: A grommet is an eyelet or ring, often rubber, lining a hole to protect a cable or rope.

clue.text: Busy period — Mike’s forgotten about self-esteem

indicators.note: what is forgotten about is left out of mind, so the letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: a month is a period of time
Mike is the radio code word for M, which is removed
your ego is your sense of self-worth

explanation.surface: A hectic spell leaves Mike neglecting his confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy period' reads as one phrase, but 'Busy' alone is the definition and 'period' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the go is constantly active, always rushing about with plenty to do.

clue.text: Jail’s image promotion has feasibility

blocks.note: PR, public relations, is the business of promoting an image
if a plan is on, it is possible; 'is on' says it has feasibility

explanation.surface: A prison's public-relations campaign is judged workable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jail's' looks possessive, but the 's is just 'is' joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison and a jail are both secure institutions where convicted criminals are confined.

clue.text: Mineral’s origin: can that’s been cracked open

indicators.note: something cracked open is broken apart, so its letters are free to settle in another arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The source of a mineral is traced to a tin that has been split open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mineral' looks like a noun, but it is an adjective meaning not from living matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Inorganic substances are those of non-living, mineral origin, the opposite of organic carbon-based matter.

clue.text: Clothes stand

blocks.note: first meaning: an outfit, often an eye-catching one
second meaning: rise to your feet

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is a noun, usually written as one word, and the second is a two-word verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A getup is an outfit or costume, and to get up is to rise from sitting or lying.

clue.text: China uncovered river creature

indicators.note: with its covers removed a thing loses its outside, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: china is fine porcelain pottery

explanation.surface: A river animal from China is found in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a sleek fish-eating mammal living along riverbanks and in streams.

clue.text: Lure politician into Vietnamese festival

indicators.note: putting something into another places it within, between that other's letters

blocks.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
Tet is the Vietnamese lunar new year celebration

explanation.surface: Someone coaxes a politician along to a Vietnamese celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Tet, the Vietnamese new year, is a handy crossword festival.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt someone is to entice or attract them towards something, as a lure does.

clue.text: Being sulky and low, eats seconds

blocks.note: to low is to make the sound a cow makes
to dine is to eat a meal
S is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: A sulky, depressed person comforts themselves by going back for second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' reads as gloomy, matching sulky, but it is the cow's verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Moodiness is the state of being given to sulks and changeable temper, a noun for being sulky.

clue.text: Government department, one fashionable in the sixties

blocks.note: first meaning: the UK Ministry of Defence
second meaning: a sharp-suited, scooter-riding youth of 1960s Britain

explanation.walkthrough: The Ministry of Defence is the British department running the armed forces; mods were a British youth subculture who clashed with rockers.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation names the UK defence ministry, and the word also names a stylish 1960s youth.

clue.text: Old man hacks into renowned computer

indicators.note: to hack into a system is to break inside it, so one piece gets within another

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
noted means famous

explanation.surface: An elderly man breaks into a famous computer system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' suggests a senior citizen, but it is slang for a father.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a small portable machine, the term once used for very light laptops.

clue.text: Establish disadvantageous position in court?

blocks.note: first meaning: to lay down or put in writing as a rule
second meaning: in tennis, trailing by one set

explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court, and the question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To set down rules is to establish them, and a player a set down is behind in a tennis match.
